Triage (first touch): **`pm:queue` + `domain:ui`**.

Landing: `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/text-input.tsx` — the `description` paragraph needs an `id` and the `Input` an `aria-describedby`. `packages/components/src/ui/input.tsx` is the primitive that does not supply it.

Graded `pm:queue`: named file, named remedy, and the `label` half of the same block is already wired correctly, so the fix has an in-file precedent to match. No open question.

objectui three-stream split (maintainer 2026-08-21). Routed via the maintainer direct-dispatch channel, this session, verbatim: 「objectui 有 79 张卡在车道视图之外（占该仓 35%），你帮我分批处理」 · 「继续 批 2 批 3」. PM session `session_0124Qg8rLvpXnQDwCmpKUmaJ`. Not a Routine triage fire — the triage seat may re-grade.

- Clause-②: **no.** A render-side a11y wiring change. No accept-set moves, no arm changes, no published name added or removed. ⚠️ It *does* touch the same file #5717 landed in two hours ago — but that card is merged and its fence released, so there is no live hold.

**Loop note:** this card was filed by #5717's dev **out of that card's fence** and correctly refused there, because the difference it records *cannot be carried by an accept-set arm*. Triage queued it; it comes back here. That is the loop working, and it is worth saying because refusing to fold a finding into an in-flight PR is what made this card exist as a clean, separately-reviewable unit.

**File surface granted (write):**

```
packages/components/src/renderers/basic/text-input.tsx
packages/components/src/__tests__/**
.changeset/*
```

Report the path first if `packages/components/src/ui/input.tsx` (the Shadcn primitive) genuinely needs to change — triage names it as the thing that *does not* supply the attribute, not as the thing to fix.

**Serial constraints:** ⛔ `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` and `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` held by **#5233**; ⛔ `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` held by **#5702**. Both in flight this round; neither overlaps `packages/components/**`.

---

⚠️ **THE CLAUSE THIS CARD CANNOT BE COMPLETE WITHOUT, and it is easy to miss:** #5717 rewrote this key's `ComponentInput.description` prose **to document the gap you are about to close**. The published text on `origin/main` currently reads:

> *"Presentational only: the renderer renders it as a sibling paragraph and does not tie it to the field with `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader does not announce it together with the input — instructions a user must not miss belong in `label`."*

**Fixing the wiring makes that sentence false**, in prose that ships to metadata authors and AI authors. Updating it is **in scope and required**, not a nicety. And the last clause — *"instructions a user must not miss belong in `label`"* — is advice that was only true *because* of the gap; re-decide whether it still belongs rather than deleting or keeping it by reflex.

**The in-file precedent to match is one line away:** the `label` half is already wired correctly (`Label htmlFor={schema?.id}` against `Input id={schema?.id}`). Follow that shape rather than inventing one — and note the asymmetry the card is really about: `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` already wires `aria-describedby` to its `FormDescription` (`:492`, `:522`, `:534`), so **one authoring key behaves two ways depending on which container the author reached for.** Read how the form renderer does it before choosing your own mechanism; converging on it is worth more than a locally clever fix.

## ACCEPT — landing. PR #5770.

Gates by name at 06:28Z (PR started 06:17:33Z): **19 `success` + 3 `skipped` = 22.** Zero `in_progress`, zero `failure`. (`Build Docs` 11 s — the path-filtered skip.)

**Fence: clean.** 3 files, all inside the grant. `packages/components/src/ui/input.tsx` was **not** edited and needs no change — it is a `forwardRef` over a native input that spreads its props, so an `aria-describedby` handed down by a caller already reaches the element. Reported rather than edited, exactly as Zone 1 required of a file named as context.

## The id question was answered better than I framed it

I framed the absent-`schema.id` path as a risk of two conventions. The answer is that there is only one, because **the two associations need ids on opposite ends**:

- `htmlFor` must name the **input**, whose id only the author can supply — so that wiring can only hold when they gave one. Unchanged.
- `aria-describedby` must name the **paragraph**, which the renderer wholly owns — so it holds **unconditionally**.

One convention — *associate where we can* — applied to a case where we always can. `React.useId()` at `:120`, the same source `FormItem` mints `formDescriptionId` from.

And the reason **not** to derive from `schema.id` is a failure mode the label wiring structurally cannot have: two nodes sharing an authored id would publish two paragraphs sharing an id, and both fields' `aria-describedby` would resolve to whichever came first — **the wrong helper text announced, which is worse than none.** Pinned by a test rather than left as reasoning.

The attribute is emitted only when a paragraph actually renders (`:125`, `description ? … : undefined`), never as a dangling reference. That **deliberately diverges** from the form path, where `FormControl`'s Slot emits it unconditionally — and the divergence is **stated in the PR rather than filed**, correctly: it is Slot-level behaviour shared with `FormMessage` and belongs to a different card.

## Zone 1b: the clause was re-decided, not deleted and not kept by reflex

The prose #5717 wrote to document this gap is rewritten in the same change — exactly one copy repo-wide, controlled.

The trailing *"instructions a user must not miss belong in `label`"* is **kept**, on a **restated and explicitly weaker basis**: a description is announced *after* the accessible name, and screen readers gate description text behind user-adjustable verbosity settings (NVDA's "Report object descriptions", VoiceOver hint verbosity, JAWS verbosity levels). And the report says the load-bearing thing about it:

> *That half is CITED, not measured … the harness proves the description is computed, never what any screen reader speaks.*

Both the code comment and the PR body carry that caveat. **Deleting the clause would have told authors that a critical instruction in `description` is now guaranteed to be heard, which nothing here can support.** That is the right call and the right disclosure.

⚠️ **My own verification instrument could not see this, and I am saying so rather than letting a count stand as evidence.** I grepped for the old sentence and got **1 on the branch, 1 on main** — which reads as "unchanged". It is not: on the branch that single occurrence is inside a **code comment at `:284` explaining that the sentence used to be true and was rewritten**. The live prose at `:296` is the new text. A count cannot tell a live claim from a quotation of its own removal.

## The ablations account for every case, which is a claim about the suite itself

Nine cases; each asserts the **relationship** — read `aria-describedby`, look each id up in the document, compare the resolved element's text — through a helper that **throws on a dangling id**, not the two attributes separately.

- **A** (remove the attribute from the Input): 7 red / 2 green. The two survivors are the absence controls, and they survive **correctly**: they assert the attribute is *absent*, which removing it cannot break — the half mutation A structurally cannot reach.
- **B** (drop the conditional so the id is always emitted): 2 red / 7 green — the exact complement.

Between them, **all nine cases die under some mutation**. That is a completeness argument about the tests, not just a pair of red lights, and it is rare.

And the stale-artifact false green is not argued away but **measured away**: `test -d packages/components/dist` exits 1, and so does `packages/core/dist` — no build artifact exists anywhere in the worktree while all nine pass. There is nothing for a stale copy to hide in.

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` ran in full (47/47 tasks, exit 0) — **no narrowing evidence owed because nothing was narrowed.**

## Two contributions beyond the card

**#5771** — `element:record_picker` renders a `label` with no `htmlFor` against a `SelectTrigger` with no id: **the association is missing at both ends**, a step worse than this card's gap, while the block's own registration prose advertises the caption as rendered "in a label element". Dedup done semantically first. Zero-hit readings controlled (`htmlFor` and `aria-` both 0 in `record-picker.tsx`; `htmlFor` returns 4 in `text-input.tsx` next door).

⚠️ **And an instrument warning that explains a session-wide symptom this seat has been working around all day:**

> *the MCP `search_issues` in this fleet is **semantic** and takes owner and repo as **parameters**. Passing GitHub search qualifiers (`repo:…`, `is:open`) inside the query string returns ZERO for everything — including terms known present in an open issue — i.e. a silent false-clean during dedup.*

That is a **mechanical explanation** for the symptom objectstack#11193 records as "search can return `total_count: 0` session-wide including control terms". It is not that search is broken; it is that qualifier syntax in a semantic query silently matches nothing. Carrying it upstream.

Zone 2d answered and correctly **not** filed: nothing else in this renderer sits in the same position — `required` reaches the native attribute, `placeholder` reaches the native attribute, and the renderer emits no error message at all, so there is no error relationship to wire.

Flipping ready → auto-merge (SQUASH).
